basisCorrection.compute: Primarily solid-state silicon computation with highly integrated functional modules.
basisCorrection.transduction: Piezoelectric sensing, actuation, vibration analysis, resonant timing and mechanically coupled interfaces are characteristic implementation choices.
basisCorrection.modularity: Ar'nock modularity is concentrated at complete functional assemblies: a replaceable module may integrate conductors, switching, capacitance, sensing, conditioning and local control that a human design would distribute across many discrete parts and boards.
basisCorrection.biotechnology: Bioprinting and biological fabrication are important secondary technologies used mainly for feedstock processing, food, medicine, environmental support and life support. They are not the default substrate for computation, propulsion, control or general machinery.
basisCorrection.supersedes: Earlier biological-symbiotic default interpretations in Ar'nock propulsion documentation. A specific biological subsystem remains allowed only where a source explicitly establishes it.

metric-envelope.physicalInvariant: The selected machinery must generate and regulate a protected metric-compression envelope; Ar'nock implementation style cannot replace metric geometry, curvature, closure or recovery requirements.
machinery: sectional solid-state field-former modules distributed around the certified envelope boundary
silicon control and estimation modules with independent timing/reference chains
piezoelectric structural-strain and vibration transducer arrays integrated into field sectors
replaceable power-conditioning and protected unwind modules
metric-envelope.power: Conditioned electrical power is distributed through modular conversion assemblies; readiness requires field-sector coherence, thermal margin and protected unwind energy in addition to gross reactor output.
metric-envelope.navigation: Family-required gravimetry and curvature estimation are solved by solid-state computation using distributed sensors; piezoelectric channels supplement structural and vibration state but do not substitute for gravimetry.
metric-envelope.control: Regional solid-state controllers balance envelope sectors through redundant deterministic buses and local abort authority.
metric-envelope.maintenance: Swap and recertify functional modules; verify connector/interface state, timing, reference agreement, piezoelectric response, thermal paths and envelope coverage. Do not assume component-level field repair is possible inside monolithic integrated modules.
metric-envelope.signature: Metric/gravitational and emergence signatures remain primary; Ar'nock-specific supporting signatures include power-conversion harmonics, switching spectra, resonant piezoelectric activity, thermal loading and mechanical vibration.
metric-envelope.failure: Envelope asymmetry, closure instability or curvature mis-solution can combine with module drift, connector damage, timing disagreement, cracked piezoelectric elements, bus isolation or cooling loss.
metric-envelope.infrastructure: No Ar'nock-specific metric corridor, beacon or calibration network is confirmed.
metric-envelope.scaling: Larger protected volumes require more independent field modules, shorter regional control loops, sectional power/cooling and local unwind authority rather than one enlarged central mechanism.
manualProcedure: verify every installed field module against current vessel geometry
compare independent solid-state reference chains before spool
reserve protected electrical and thermal unwind capacity
abort before commit if a required field sector cannot isolate or maintain envelope continuity

gravitic-plane.physicalInvariant: The drive must couple the vessel to usable gravitational/shear terrain and survive branch, gradient and tidal conditions; implementation style cannot turn gravity terrain into an unconstrained lane.
machinery: long-baseline gravimetric sensor modules tied to rigid surveyed baselines
sectional gravitic coupling modules tied into structural load paths
piezoelectric strain/vibration arrays for differential-load measurement and alignment diagnostics
gravitic-plane.power: Power burden is dominated by sensing, coupling, recoupling, control and recovery rather than a simple speed-to-reactor relation.
gravitic-plane.navigation: Independent solid-state sensor chains reconstruct gradients, tides, shear forks and branch solutions while retaining covariance and source ancestry.
gravitic-plane.control: Regional controllers coordinate coupling while local strain measurements prevent vessel-average readings from hiding destructive differential loading.
gravitic-plane.maintenance: Survey sensor baselines, coupling-module alignment, structural attachments, piezoelectric calibration, reference-clock agreement and emergency decoupling paths.
gravitic-plane.signature: Gravitational coupling remains family-primary; supporting evidence includes electrical load steps, timing traffic, structural resonance and piezoelectric diagnostic activity.
gravitic-plane.failure: A bad terrain solution or shear fork can combine with correlated sensor bias, cracked transducers, timing drift, damaged bus segments or coupling-module misalignment.
gravitic-plane.infrastructure: No Ar'nock gravitational-terrain observatory or surveyed corridor network is confirmed.
gravitic-plane.scaling: Mass distribution and vessel span increase differential-coupling burden; capital hulls require regional sensors, local load-aware coupling modules and sectional decoupling authority.
manualProcedure: prove sensor independence before accepting a branch solution
compare coupling load and piezoelectric strain by hull region
isolate modules reporting unsupported certainty
recouple only while family-specific decision horizon remains

slipstream-shear.physicalInvariant: The vessel must acquire, adhere to, forecast and safely detach from a Q-boundary shear; an Ar'nock implementation remains a boundary-riding system, not a generic warp drive.
machinery: forward Q-state sensor modules with independent references
protected electrical detachment and recovery modules
slipstream-shear.power: Acquisition, hold, correction, sensing, compute, cooling and protected detachment reserve are separately budgeted.
slipstream-shear.navigation: Solid-state estimators forecast Q-weather, boundary curvature, wake state, exit correspondence and adhesion margin beyond immediate detection range.
slipstream-shear.control: Sectional modules trim local coupling while redundant supervisory processors protect whole-hull coherence and exit options.
slipstream-shear.maintenance: Inspect coupling-module calibration, connector integrity, timing drift, sensor contamination, piezoelectric alignment diagnostics and detachment-path isolation.
slipstream-shear.signature: Q-boundary and wake signatures remain primary; Ar'nock supporting evidence includes switching spectra, field-module harmonics, thermal load and resonant diagnostics.
slipstream-shear.failure: Adhesion deficit, Q-weather, boundary pinch or exit loss can combine with module drift, bus damage, reference disagreement or inadequate recovery reserve.
slipstream-shear.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-weather network or surveyed slipstream corridor is confirmed.
slipstream-shear.scaling: Increasing hull area multiplies coupling sectors and finite control latency; regional autonomous solid-state controllers become increasingly important.
manualProcedure: map installed coupling coverage after hull changes
validate forward sensing through independent reference chains
protect detachment reserve from route optimization
detach before local module or forecast uncertainty consumes the safety horizon

q-lattice.physicalInvariant: The installation must solve discrete Q address and epoch validity with complete protected-state coverage; ordinary distance cannot substitute for lattice adjacency.
machinery: redundant silicon epoch-clock and reference assemblies
q-lattice.power: Energy is allocated separately to address lock, phase alignment, coverage, translation, exit and protected recovery.
q-lattice.navigation: Silicon computation maintains address hypotheses, epoch windows, alias uncertainty, references and destination exclusion without averaging incompatible candidates into false certainty.
q-lattice.control: Independent timing modules preserve clock ancestry and reject regional desynchronization before commit.
q-lattice.maintenance: Recertify cage coverage, clock phase, resonator response, connector state, local reference stability and cargo/appendage inclusion after refit.
q-lattice.signature: Q-state preparation remains family-primary; supporting signatures can include resonant electrical sweeps, timing synchronization traffic, thermal load and piezoelectric reference activity.
q-lattice.failure: Address alias, epoch miss, coverage hole, clock split or reference poisoning can be worsened by oscillator drift, fractured transducers, module mismatch or bad refit provenance.
q-lattice.infrastructure: No Ar'nock Q-address beacon or lattice index network is confirmed.
q-lattice.scaling: The weakest local cage region controls validity; large hulls require redundant local cage modules and independent timing authorities rather than stronger average coverage.
manualProcedure: enumerate every carried structure inside the protected-state definition
compare epoch clocks through independent reference ancestry
reject unresolved address aliases
hold recovery capacity outside discretionary translation energy

n-manifold.physicalInvariant: The system must select a higher-dimensional route while preserving an admissible return map; implementation style cannot replace dimensional topology or return conditioning.
n-manifold.power: Embedding, axis control, sensing, inference, route solution, return conditioning, cooling and protected re-embedding capacity are separately budgeted.
n-manifold.navigation: Independent compute modules estimate higher-dimensional obstacles, axis state, route geometry, return conditioning and ordinary-space emergence covariance.
n-manifold.control: Regional controllers maintain embedding coherence while independent return authority prevents route optimization and recovery from sharing one failure ancestry.
n-manifold.maintenance: Test axis/parity response, reference modules, embedding coverage, tomography residuals, compute-module version identity and sectional recovery hardware.
n-manifold.signature: Topology/embedding and emergence evidence remain primary; supporting evidence includes high-rate compute/power activity, thermal load, switching spectra and reference-resonator excitation.
n-manifold.failure: Axis inversion, hidden obstacles or return-map divergence can combine with compute corruption, timing disagreement, module-version mismatch or damaged reference transducers.
n-manifold.infrastructure: No Ar'nock manifold survey network is confirmed.
n-manifold.scaling: Additional hull span and active axes increase control and model complexity; mature implementations require hierarchical local control and an independently maintained return system.
manualProcedure: verify minimum sufficient active dimensionality
treat coherent unexplained tomography residuals as unresolved obstacles
audit return-map evidence independently
retain re-embedding reserve even when a shorter route is available

fold-jump.physicalInvariant: The installation must create temporary topological adjacency between certified origin and destination volumes and obey its precommit point of no return; no control architecture creates post-commit steering authority.
machinery: modular solid-state topology-former assemblies around the certified volume
fold-jump.power: Event energy is divided among nucleation, shaping, holding, closure/ringing control and protected recovery.
fold-jump.navigation: Endpoint covariance, destination occupancy, gravity conditioning, source authentication and topology bifurcation remain explicit.
fold-jump.control: Solid-state solvers may continuously re-solve before commit but hard-veto invented steering after topology execution begins.
fold-jump.maintenance: Survey protected-volume geometry, topology-former modules, endpoint reference ancestry, timing, closure response and refit identity.
fold-jump.signature: Topological transient and closure signatures remain primary; supporting signatures include capacitor/buffer charging, clock synchronization, field-former switching and heat rejection.
fold-jump.failure: Endpoint covariance, occupancy conflict, topology bifurcation or premature commit can combine with coverage-module dropout, timing drift or closure-reserve isolation.
fold-jump.infrastructure: No Ar'nock fold beacon or prepared endpoint infrastructure is confirmed.
fold-jump.scaling: Larger volumes magnify boundary certification and closure burden; sectional modularity improves serviceability but does not relax destination exclusion.
manualProcedure: prove the destination as a clear volume, not a coordinate
freeze protected-volume geometry before final solution
protect closure and recovery reserve
abort before commit when covariance or evidence ancestry becomes unacceptable

wormhole-gate.physicalInvariant: The installation must maintain a synchronized multiply connected throat with finite aperture, mass flux, remote-mouth state and chronology protection; gate machinery is infrastructure, not a ship drive enlarged by assumption.
machinery: modular aperture-former sectors in a rigid surveyed support ring
authenticated paired-mouth silicon reference and timing networks
industrial power, thermal and protected closure modules
wormhole-gate.power: Hold, shape, synchronization, traffic, thermal and protected closure/recovery loads remain separately accounted.
wormhole-gate.navigation: Remote-mouth authentication and measured synchronization remain distinct from prediction; stale inferred remote state cannot be presented as current measurement.
wormhole-gate.control: Regional aperture modules regulate throat geometry and mass flux while chronology veto and independent closure authority remain non-negotiable.
wormhole-gate.maintenance: Inspect anchor geometry, modular aperture sectors, timing/reference networks, cooling, traffic-load damage, piezoelectric structural diagnostics and closure stores at both mouths.
wormhole-gate.signature: Persistent throat/topological signatures remain primary; supporting evidence includes industrial electrical demand, thermal rejection, switching harmonics and structural resonances.
wormhole-gate.failure: Throat instability, desynchronization, asymmetric mass flux, chronology trip or anchor drift can combine with module dropout, bus partition, timing disagreement or thermal saturation.
wormhole-gate.infrastructure: The family is inherently infrastructure-heavy, but Ar'nock ownership of any gate network remains UNRESOLVED.
wormhole-gate.scaling: Aperture area, mass flux, synchronization, anchoring, cooling and traffic control scale independently; never model a strategic gate as a shipboard module multiplied only by size.
manualProcedure: authenticate both mouths through independent evidence
certify aperture and traffic envelope
reserve controlled closure capacity before admission
veto passage on chronology, synchronization or remote-state uncertainty

phase-displacement.physicalInvariant: The installation must map a protected macroscopic state to an admissible nonlocal target while preserving the family's continuity and exclusion invariants; implementation style cannot waive those invariants.
machinery: protected coherence, rejection and recovery assemblies
phase-displacement.power: Preparation, coherence, target compatibility, displacement, rejection and protected recovery remain separately budgeted.
phase-displacement.navigation: Independent processors maintain target compatibility, exclusion evidence, state covariance and reference integrity through the precommit interval.
phase-displacement.control: Regional phase modules synchronize against independent clocks and references; disagreement blocks commit rather than being averaged away.
phase-displacement.maintenance: Verify module revision identity, clock/reference agreement, geometric coverage, resonant transducer calibration, power isolation and recovery stores after every major refit.
phase-displacement.signature: Family-specific phase/displacement evidence remains primary; supporting evidence can include synchronization traffic, resonant sweeps, switching transients and thermal preparation.
phase-displacement.failure: Coverage loss, incompatible target state, reference corruption or rejection failure can combine with timing drift, module mismatch, fractured transducers or power partition.
phase-displacement.infrastructure: No Ar'nock phase-navigation infrastructure is confirmed.
phase-displacement.scaling: Larger protected states require more sectional phase modules and tighter timing/reference discipline; modularity limits fault propagation but does not relax continuity requirements.
manualProcedure: verify complete protected-state geometry
prove independent clock/reference agreement
preserve rejection and recovery stores
block commit on unresolved module-version or target-compatibility disagreement

generatorContract.selectionRule: Species identity never selects an FTL family. A family must come from named canon or explicit caller/scenario selection.
generatorContract.outputStatus: Caller-selected family plus Ar'nock embodiment is MIXED.
generatorContract.provenanceRule: Every generated installation preserves family source, Ar'nock technology-profile source, association source, module/refit ancestry and any biological exception source separately.
generatorContract.unknownRule: Missing Ar'nock family, manufacturer, performance, latency, connector standard or infrastructure remains UNRESOLVED; generators may not fill it with biological assumptions.
generatorContract.basisRule: Default Ar'nock general machinery to solid-state electromechanical modular construction with silicon computation and piezoelectric sensing/actuation. Apply biotechnology only to feedstock, medicine, environmental/life support, or a specifically sourced biological subsystem.

canonSafeguards: Ar'nock technology is not generically biological or symbiotic.
Bioprinting does not imply biological computation, biological propulsion or living field machinery.
Default Ar'nock compute to solid-state silicon and general machinery to modular electromechanical/solid-state assemblies.
Piezoelectric functions may support sensing, actuation, vibration analysis, structural diagnostics and timing without replacing family-required exotic sensors.
Species identity does not assign an FTL family.
Same family mathematics does not imply the same machinery embodiment.
A caller-selected family remains MIXED rather than confirmed Ar'nock ownership.
Legacy biological-default text is superseded where it conflicts with this corrected profile.
